expected.summary: The practice board with GND planes on layers 1 and 2, stitching vias and a top soldermask opening, drawn from the top into a new PNG; exists reads back true and the result counts the pads, traces, planes and openings drawn on the layers and side drawn, and every via.
Only layer 2, which holds nothing but its plane, is drawn: a valid picture of the outline, the plane and the vias, and the result counts no pad, no trace and the one plane of layer 2.
The session has no such board open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

rows.reason: pcb render writes only a new picture file and changes nothing in Layout, so no lock or changed state of the board stands in its way; a picture file that exists already raises the tier to two-step instead.

expected.summary: Run under a scope file that does not cover the output folder; nothing is drawn.

While a forward-annotation run or pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout, the session reports busy or unresponsive. Only --session is given: Layout does not say which board it has open while it does not answer, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout before the call, such as Setup > Setup Parameters or Help > About. Layout may go on answering COM, so a dialog box over it, or a Layout that stops answering, is reported as the session blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a Layout that stops answering does not say which board it has open.
Layout goes away while the board is read; no picture is written.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: The board holds unsaved changes: it is drawn as it stands in Layout's memory, from the bottom.
The call waits before its read-back, and meanwhile the picture file is deleted (--tamper), so exists reads back false.
